summary: A set of checkboxes answering one question. Owns the selected values, the group's label, help and error, and "select at least one".
useWhen: several options may be picked and they answer one question — "notify me when", "regions", "columns to show"
the group needs a rule of its own — at least one, or an error that belongs to the set rather than to an option

useInstead.when: only one option may be picked
the options are many, or space is tight
useInstead.why: past about seven options a list of boxes is longer than the form around it; MultiSelect filters them and shows the chosen ones as tags
a group of one announces a question and then its only answer

useInstead.when: each option needs a sentence to be chosen well, and several can be
useInstead.why: the same group with tiles for its options: each a real checkbox the size of a card, its sentence read after its name

composition.note: Give every Checkbox a `value`; the group's `onChange` receives the array of ticked values. Selection lives on the group — do not also set `isSelected` on the boxes.
composition.example: <CheckboxGroup label="Notify the team when" isRequired value={notifyOn} onChange={setNotifyOn} isInvalid={!!error} errorMessage={error}><Checkbox value="failed">A run fails</Checkbox><Checkbox value="approval">A run needs approval</Checkbox></CheckboxGroup>

neutral.use: facts rather than approvals — the columns shown, the filters applied

vertical.use: the default, and always when a label runs past a few words

horizontal.use: two to four one-word options — weekdays, regions. Wraps rather than overflows

label.note: renders as the <legend> — the question the options answer

description.note: help beneath the options; replaced by `errorMessage` while `isInvalid` is set

guarantees: the legend is announced as the group's name when focus enters any box
the description or error is on every box's `aria-describedby` as well as the fieldset's, so it is read on the box that takes focus

`isRequired` sets native `required` on every box while none is ticked and on none once one is: the browser blocks the submit in its own language, and each box announces "required" exactly while the rule is unmet
`isDisabled` cascades to every Checkbox that has not set its own
requires: `label`, or `aria-label` when the question is already visible elsewhere
a `value` on every Checkbox — the group tracks the selection by it

antiPatterns.dont: loose Checkboxes under a text label
antiPatterns.why: the question is not announced with the options, an error has nothing to attach to, and "at least one" cannot be expressed

antiPatterns.dont: `isSelected` or `checked` on a Checkbox inside a group
antiPatterns.why: the group owns the selection; the box's own value is ignored

antiPatterns.dont: `isRequired` on every Checkbox in the group
antiPatterns.why: that means every box must be ticked; `isRequired` on the group means at least one
